title: Taiwanese American Student Association at UCLA
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Student Association (TASA) at UCLA is a student organization established on October 31, 2011. Its mission, as stated in the UCLA Community club directory, is to spread Taiwanese awareness and culture through community involvement and to build and strengthen the Taiwanese American community on campus. TASA describes itself as open to Taiwanese students, Taiwanese Americans, and anyone with an interest in Taiwanese culture.

TASA organizes events throughout the academic year, including food workshops, movie nights, retreats, and outings across Los Angeles. The organization also runs a Taiwanese American Heritage Week (TAHW) each May, a two-week series of events dedicated to educating the broader community about Taiwan and its culture. Internally, TASA uses a “fam system” that divides the membership into smaller groups, as well as a big-little mentorship pairing between upperclassmen and newer members.

TASA has collaborated with TSA and other Southern California Taiwanese student organizations — including those at USC, UCSB, UCI, and UCSD — through an annual Taiwanese Field Trip Invitational (TFTI). In 2022, TASA revived its Taiwanese Culture Night (TCN) after a four-year hiatus, co-producing a theatrical performance with TSA. TASA is listed as an active organization in UCLA’s official Community club directory and maintains an active Instagram (@uclatasa) with over 1,900 followers.
